positions.title: Software Engineer, Data Governance
highlights: Built React and Django internal web application that automates Databricks onboarding — users submit forms and the application executes Databricks API calls to provision workspace access, create Azure AD groups, and manage group membership
Administer Databricks platform across multiple workspaces, including user access provisioning, service principals, catalog permissions, external volumes, and Azure storage integration

positions.title: Data Engineer, Connected Vehicle Data Engineering
highlights: Designed and deployed event-driven data collection systems, processing real-time telemetry across GM's connected vehicle fleet

Resolved production data collection failures for rental fleet partner (100,000+ vehicles) by implementing direct read method to bypass queue bottleneck, ensuring accurate fuel level and odometer telemetry
Developed Python ETL pipeline migrating CSV/XML configuration files from Git repository into Databricks, enabling PowerBI analytics for deployed data collection programs

positions.title: Software Engineer, Big Data Engineering & Infrastructure
highlights: Developed GM's custom Hadoop distribution (GMDP) by integrating open-source components including Tez UI, Ambari, and Livy, migrating from Cloudera and reducing annual costs by $1.2M
Contributed to Apache Ambari and Bigtop open-source projects by implementing Livy service integration (Ambari PR#3790, Bigtop PR#1282)
Automated Docker-based Hadoop development environment, reducing developer setup time from 35+ minutes to 10 minutes by eliminating manual build and deployment steps
Responded to Log4Shell vulnerability by developing automated remediation script for production Hadoop clusters, integrating into standard startup process for ongoing protection

projects.name: Coaster: E-Ink Cycling GPS
highlights: Designing and building an ESP32-S3 cycling computer with a 200x200 e-paper display that records rides from GPS and barometer sensors to GPX files and uploads them to Strava when it reaches home Wi-Fi

projects.name: Real-Time Transit Data Pipeline
highlights: Python service polling the 511.org transit API every minute for real-time San Francisco Muni arrival predictions, storing them in PostgreSQL and visualizing arrivals and route maps in Grafana dashboards
Containerized with Docker and deployed to Kubernetes on an Oracle Cloud server as a scheduled CronJob alongside PostgreSQL and Grafana
